summary: The service started this run, not an instruction: the last width-200 baseline loop (f* 0.38, job 164691, unmodified engine with friction) had ended. There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. No time went to unasked work. The onset pilot serves the experiment's own registered test. One sentence is wrong, and it is in the line state Chris reads first. The L0018 state in ledger/lines.jsonl says 'Over the ten baseline loops, width 200 never reached further in Gamma than width 100.' The headline ('the wider box never reached further in Gamma than the paper's box'), the summary of evidence/E0076-results.json ('At no end did width 200 reach further than width 100'), PROGRAM.md and lines/L0018/progress.md say the same. It is false at the f* 0.50 floor. Width 200 completed Gamma 2.35, and width 100 stopped on its cap at 2.35 with a floor of 2.4, so width 200 went 0.05 further down. Both ends there are CPU cap stops, so this is not evidence for the wider box. But the blanket sentence is wrong as written. It should say 'at no end where the comparison means something (a physical stop at both widths, or a one-sided stop)'. Everything else I checked reproduces. All forty-five per-step entries for the f* 0.38 loop in evidence/E0076-interim.json match the mirrored summary.json files: SHA-256, Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow stretches, with zero mismatches. The range is 2.45 to 4.0, with forty-three completed steps. The floor stop is a two CPU-hour cap at 2.4 after twenty-three cycles. The top stop is an eight CPU-hour cap at 4.05 after seventeen cycles. The steps sum to 65.16 CPU-hours, against 65.53 in the job record. The cost per cycle at 4.05 is 14.0 times that at 4.0. No step gained energy, failed the audit or had a slow stretch, so the referee check on slow_episodes is clean. I fetched all ten width-100 ramp.jsonl files from A0068. The f* 0.38 one matches its recorded SHA-256. Every width-100 floor, top and stop type in the working-range table reproduces. So does the width-100 f* 0.38 top: a frozen-time stop at 4.05 after nine cycles, with three slow episodes and a cost per cycle 16.8 times that of the 4.0 step. The width-200 columns match the interim loops. The ten job records sum to 343.62 CPU-hours. I recomputed one onset-pilot row from the raw fields.npz (width 100, Gamma 2.45). Its SHA-256 matches, and so do the largest and smallest phase variances, the amplitude (0.388) and the dominant ring (k = 2, share 0.214). I have one caution about the pilot's reading, not an error in it. 'Regained at 2.65 in the paper's box and 2.7 in the wide box' is a difference at the resolution of the measure. The rings are spaced 2 pi / L apart, so width 100 cannot resolve wavelengths between 33 and 25 diameters, and width 200 can. Read as a wavelength, the way up runs nearly in step at both widths: 50, 50, 33 and 25 diameters at Gamma 2.5 to 2.65 at width 100, and 40, 40, 33, 29 and 25 at 2.5 to 2.7 at width 200. Also, the pattern ring's share of the variance is lower at width 200 (0.3 to 0.54) than at width 100 (0.5 to 0.76), because a ring at larger k holds more modes. So the rule in proposed direction one, 'carries most of the height variance', would make the wide box look unpatterned at most steps. The rule should judge dominance by wavelength in diameters, not by ring index or by a share above one half. All three points from my previous review were answered. (1) The up-leg cap proposal is withdrawn, and the width-100 cost jump near Gamma 3.35 is recorded. (2) 11.4 is now written for f* 0.57. (3) The ledger timestamps (05:51Z) are earlier than the run's end (05:52:52Z) and its commit (05:53:22Z). program check passes. It still lists approved/20261124T031934297997Z (Nov 24 03:19) as the latest approval, which I reported before. It counts 561.4 of 10000 CPU-hours this week. The job records that ended since Nov 19 sum to 801.5, so the run's hedge of 'about 800' is right, and program check undercounts ended jobs. sequel-data is 678 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. tmp/ was empty after I deleted my own fetches, and active.jsonl is empty. Outside the two allowed folders, the only writes in the run's window are pytest and uv scratch in ~/.tmp (the environment's TMPDIR, from the referee test run) and the harness's own folder. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a twelve-minute service run, from 05:41:08 to 05:52:52 by its own record, committed at 05:53:22. It started four minutes after the line's job ended and the CLAUDE.md sync at 05:37. It collected the one ended loop, built the all-frequency working-range table, answered my three points and ran a one-frequency onset pilot. It started nothing, cancelled nothing and left no jobs running locally. Nineteen width-200 loops are still on Hatteras: ten without friction (E0074) and nine with the nudge (E0075). The host is a Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be measured. The summary says so, and it gives the load from /proc/loadavg instead. The interruption it reports is plausible but I could not confirm it from the machine: the L0015 run was working in the same window, until its commit at 05:45, and could have emptied the shared fetch folder. Local CPU was a few minutes of fetching and reading, so 0.05 CPU-hours is about right. Free disk of 92 gigabytes at both ends matches the 91 I see now. The machine did not limit the science. The loops' own CPU caps set four floors at both widths and one width-200 top, and the run says this is a limit of the design.
discrepancies: scheduled_start is the time the agent noted, not a measured runner start, as the summary itself says.
The fetch-folder interruption (05:44:30 to 05:46:30, times approximate) could not be checked against anything on the machine.
